{detail} - Marked ok and nothing written down: settled in name only. The decision has to reach the card, or it is lost when this session ends.
{detail} - An answer was read and never marked ok or not-ok, so nobody can tell whether it settled the question.
{detail} - The owner has answered and I have not read it. He answers from his phone and then waits; an answer nobody acts on is the same to him as no answer.

{detail} - Nothing on this board has moved for three days. The age is deliberately generous: this board legitimately sits still while it is blocked on the owner, and a rule that fires while correctly blocked teaches its reader to skim - which is worse than not having the rule.
{detail} - The board has not been backed up. Retiring the previous tracker nearly lost the most consequential open finding in the project; the gate trails live in the comments, not in the commits.

{detail} - Police has been writing and nobody has read it. On 2026-08-15 two hundred violations had piled up across a full day, and the only thing that surfaced it was the owner asking whether the bridge was monitored. A channel nobody listens on is silent in exactly the way a quiet one is.

{detail} - This card is being worked without the detail the ticket gate requires. SCOPE, PLAN, acceptance criteria, test steps, BDD and ATDD are written BEFORE implementation, because criteria written afterwards describe what was built instead of deciding whether it is right.

{detail} - A card reached the released column without recording WHICH version shipped it. Reconstructing that for 45 cards took two-source git archaeology on 10 August; the field would have made it a lookup.

{detail} - A card being worked must record the work tree it is worked in, under /home/mv/dd-worktree-sandbox. Police reads this project's declared repository now, so a report of a missing branch or tree is about the card rather than about where police was started - which is exactly what made this rule unusable before and got it declined.
{detail} - a finished checklist on a card that has not moved. The work is done and the column still says otherwise, which is the drift that makes a board stop describing reality.

{detail} - Nothing has happened to this card for longer than its column allows. On a single-agent board the failure this catches is mine: a card claimed, worked for a while, and left behind when something louder arrived. The column sets its own limit where it has one; 6h is the fallback, matching the threshold FT99 already uses for a card in a working column.
{detail} - A working column claims somebody is working this. Assign it or move it out - this exact drift has been caught by the owner from a phone screenshot more than once.

{detail} - A checklist standing still while the card is being worked is the acceptance criteria going stale: the card claims progress the criteria do not confirm. Declined on 2026-08-14 on the ground that this project does not use checklists - three cards were already carrying them that day, so the premise was false when written. Declared again because checklists are where acceptance criteria are tracked here.
declared.was_declined: Declined 2026-08-14 on a premise that was FALSE WHEN WRITTEN - DD-495 (2026-08-08), DD-501 and DD-502 (2026-08-09) already carried checklists. Restored 2026-08-16 after decline-watch reported the condition fired. Flood test before restoring: 194 cards, 10 with checklists, 9 of them terminal, so exactly one non-terminal card can be reported.

declared.message: {detail} - This card moved into a working column while its checklist stood still. Progress claimed by dragging is the failure this board exists to prevent - a column is a claim about what is true, and moving one without doing the work makes it a false one.

{detail} - A card reached the git gate without passing through the gates this project's SDLC requires. CVE-free and a green suite are per-ticket gates here, not optional stages, and a card that arrives at the commit without them has skipped the evidence rather than the ceremony.

{detail} - A working column with no rule scoped to it is a column where a card can rest indefinitely with nothing to say so. This rule found eleven such columns here, including all four gate columns. It was declined for one day because it also named the three columns where work ENDS; upstream narrowed it in 2.34 (TKT-239) and it is declared again.
declared.was_declined: Declined 2026-08-15 because it named this board three TERMINAL columns, where nothing truthful can be declared. Restored 2026-08-16 when Tira 2.34 landed TKT-239. Upstream records that the rule DID already check for endings and got the arithmetic wrong across three boards - so the original report, that it did not skip them, was right about the symptom and wrong about the cause.

declared.message: {detail} - Every commit title carries its DD-NNN. A commit that names no card cannot be traced back to the work that justified it.

{detail} - The card has been talked about since it was last written down. On this project the talking happens on Telegram and in this session, both of which vanish; only the card survives. Seven decisions were found settled and lost this way in a single sweep.
{detail} - Work set aside with no reason recorded. A discarded card with no explanation is indistinguishable from one abandoned by accident, and the next reader cannot tell which.
{detail} - A card set aside while it still carries a question nobody answered. The question leaves with the card and stops waiting, so it is never answered and never visibly abandoned either.
{detail} - A gate is not passed until its record exists. This card reached the git gate with no gate recorded, so there is nothing a stranger could check.

{detail} - The Windows QEMU E2E container is still running. It is a full Windows virtual machine started detached, so a leaked one holds real memory and CPU for as long as nobody looks. The pattern is our own container name so another project's containers are never implicated.
{detail} - A suite run has been alive for hours. On 11 August one sat wedged for 1 day 20 hours holding seven processes, producing no failure and no last line, and was read as healthy progress.

{detail} - A headless browser from a smoke test is still running. This is the exact process that wedged the 11 August gate; the pattern is narrowed to our own dump-dom smoke so another project's browsers are never implicated.

{detail} - A parent is claiming to be finished above a child that is not. An epic once sat parked while eight of its children were built and six shipped, and was then asked to verify an assembled result it had never seen.

{detail} - A lower-priority card is being worked while a higher-priority one waits untouched. Single agent here, so this is always a choice - and being passed over does not ripen, which is why the rule has no age.
{detail} - A question has been waiting on you. The grace is deliberately long so this never nags overnight.

{detail} - A rule nobody has decided on is a rule nobody is applying, and this board has proved it: four upgrade notices arrived in one day and none was acted on, while a rule sat undeclared the whole time. Declining counts as deciding - what is not allowed is leaving it unconsidered.
{detail} - Commits are pushed per finished ticket. Work that exists only on this machine is work nobody else can see and a machine failure can erase.
{detail} - Single-agent project, and full-suite verification is host-exclusive. One card in flight at a time; a second means one of them is not being carried.
{detail} - No work starts without a ticket. The tree is changing while no card is at a working gate, so whatever is being done is unrecorded.

declined.reason:
"Still declined, but NOT for the reason first recorded - that one has been overtaken. It was declined on 2026-08-14 because the rule reported any parentless card and standalone tickets are the norm here by design. TKT-269 (Tira 2.35) fixed precisely that: orphan-card now honours the standalone label, which the command reference defines as saying somebody meant the card to have none. So the original objection no longer applies.
It stays declined for a NEW and measured reason: 191 cards on this board, 156 parentless, 3 carrying the label - so re-declaring today reports 153 historical cards. That is the gate-missing flood again, reverted as 00dddbc, and a rule that reports the same unactionable thing for ever is worse than no rule on a channel somebody reads.
Deliberately NOT fixed by bulk-labelling those 153: the label asserts that somebody MEANT a card to be parentless, and applying it to cards nobody has judged would be a bulk claim dressed as a fact.
RE-DECLARE WHEN the count of parentless cards WITHOUT the standalone label falls to roughly the cards raised since this decision - i.e. once new cards are reliably labelled at creation (CLAUDE.md now requires it) and the historical remainder has been judged or retired. That is reachable and countable with tira.export --fields ref,parent,labels, unlike a trigger naming a state the board can never enter.

RE-DECLARE TRIGGER: standalone-labelling-caught-up"

"Most cards here genuinely depend on nothing, so requiring a dependency link would manufacture false relationships to satisfy a checker - which is worse than no rule, because an invented link is indistinguishable from a real one afterwards. Real blocks are recorded when they exist, as DD-532 is on DD-534.\n\nRE-DECLARE TRIGGER: none  (deliberately permanent: most cards here genuinely depend on nothing, and requiring a dependency would manufacture false relationships. This is a settled decision, not one awaiting a condition - declared explicitly so a watcher can tell it apart from a decline nobody has revisited.)"

note: The policy set this project decided. policy-sweep reconciles the live board against this hourly. A rule DECLINED on the board is never restored from here: a decline is a decision with a reason attached and is more recent than this file.
